title: Proof of wenzl bridge applicability qou
html:
Proof.

Step 1 (Schur--Weyl setup). Self-duality of A and rigidity of \mathbf{C} give a braided monoidal action of the braid group B_n on V^{\otimes n}. Tannaka--Krein reconstruction realises \mathbf{C} \simeq \mathbf{Rep}(H), so the centraliser of the diagonal H-action on V^{\otimes n} is the Hecke algebra of type A_{n-1}:

  H_n(R, q) \;=\; \mathrm{End}_H(V^{\otimes n}),

with multiplicity decomposition V^{\otimes n} \cong \bigoplus_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n} V_\lambda^H \otimes V_\lambda^{H_n} where \dim_R V_\lambda^{H_n} = d_\lambda is the classical Hecke irrep dimension.

Step 2 (fibre-functor trace = Markov trace). The fibre-functor trace on \mathrm{End}_R(V^{\otimes n}), restricted to the H_n(R, q)-summand under the decomposition of Step 1, satisfies the Markov property \mathrm{tr}(x \cdot \sigma_n) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}(x) for x \in H_n — a direct consequence of the braided monoidal partial-trace identity for right-hand closure. Under the integer-power Hecke presentation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 on the rank-2 fundamental V of quantum dimension [2]_q = q + q^{-1} (r = 2, Q = q^2), the partial trace fixes the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2 + 1) = q^2/[2]_q (matching z_{\mathrm{GL}} = q\,z = Q^2(1 - Q)/(1 - Q^2) in Step 4 below).

Step 3 (uniqueness of the trace). By Chlouveraki HDR Theorem 6.20 (equivalently Juyumaya's Theorem 12 at d = 1), the type-A Markov-trace family on \{H_n(R, q)\}_{n \ge 1} is one-dimensional in the trace functionals — the conditions (a) trace property, (b) Markov property at parameter z, (c) consistency across the tower H_n \hookrightarrow H_{n+1} together cut out a one-parameter family parameterised by z (volume normalisation). The normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 pins the scale.

Step 4 (Wenzl bridge supplies the closed form). The g-convention isomorphism g_i := q \sigma_i transports \mathrm{tr}_M on \sigma-Hecke (with the framework's z) to \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{GL}} on g-Hecke (with z_{\mathrm{GL}} = q \cdot z). By Wenzl 1988, the Markov trace on g-Hecke at z_{\mathrm{GL}} = Q^r(1 - Q)/(1 - Q^r) has weights \omega_\lambda(Q) = s_{\lambda, r}(Q) given by the principal Schur specialisation, where Q = q^2. Combining Steps 1--3 with this formula yields the Wenzl-bridge closed form (13.28.4):

  y_\lambda \;=\;
  \frac{s_\lambda(1, Q, Q^2, \ldots, Q^{r - 1})}
       {\sum_{\mu \,\vdash\, n} d_\mu \cdot s_\mu(1, Q, Q^2, \ldots, Q^{r - 1})}.

The trace is forced, not assumed: every step is dictated by the QOU substrate axioms plus the Chlouveraki HDR uniqueness theorem. \square

Satisfaction of the hypotheses by the QOU substrate

Hypothesis QOU realisation
Rigid braided monoidal category \mathbf{C} as the rigid braided monoidal category of QOU
Self-dual fundamental object A as the fundamental confined particle, self-dual via A^* \cong A from the antipode
Fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to R\text{-mod} realising the state bundle
Tannaka--Krein Hopf algebra H = U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) in the running QOU example
V = \tau(A) has q-dimension [2]_q = q + q^{-1} (r = 2) direct from A being the spin-\tfrac{1}{2} representation, fixing z = q^2/[2]_q = q^3/(q^2 + 1)
